observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South and east show a lean, long-legged bird that stands like a ground runner. It has charcoal-grey plumage, saturated orange feather edges, a spiky crest and a long tail fanned in orange-tipped plumes. North is a different-looking bird: an upright, broad-shouldered eagle seen from behind, perched with its wings folded. It is noticeably taller than the others, has a short, wide, pointed tail, and its head is turned in profile to the right so the hooked beak shows. The north view also has a heavier black outline and flatter, more graphic shading than south and east.
observed.south.png: Front view of the bird standing. The face is toward the camera: hooked beak pointing down, two small eyes and an orange spiky crest. The orange breast streak runs down a grey body. The thin legs have large dark talons. The tail sweeps out to the viewer's left, so the pose is slightly three-quarter. There is no twig and no flame. The background is clean transparent alpha.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The bird is gaunt, with a long neck, a spiky swept-back crest, an amber eye and a hooked beak. It is mid-stride on long, thin legs, with a very long trailing tail of grey and orange plumes. The wings are folded along the back. The orange reads as flat bright fringes on the feathers; nothing glows. It carries no twig. Alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view of an upright, stocky, eagle-like bird. The back shows chevron feathers, the folded wings are symmetric with large orange edging, the tail is short, wide and fanned, and the talons poke out at the sides. The head is turned to the right in profile, with the hooked beak and the side of the face visible. The silhouette is much bulkier than south/east, it is taller (238 px against 192), the tail shape is different, and the outline is a heavy dark keyline. Alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the bird stands beside the vanilla human and is about as long as the human is tall, but shorter and lower to the ground. It reads as a large raptor. At 32 px per cell it is a small dark-and-orange bird shape with a visible tail, about rat-sized but longer.
observed.flight_1.png: Six east flight frames. f0 is a different drawing: a smaller, softer, painterly bird with a long trailing tail and wings raised, and its body is placed and posed differently. f1–f5 share a heavier-keylined, cel-like body with a short tail, and the wings sweep from up to down. In f3–f4 the wing overlays smear across the body, so the body outline changes. None of the frames shows a twig.
observed.flight_2.png: Five north flight frames. A spread-winged bird seen from behind. Its head shows in a small profile or rear view at the top. The body and tail hold still while the wings move from raised to level. It has a heavy black keyline and bright orange, a sticker-like look.
observed.flight_3.png: Five south flight frames. Front view of a spread-winged bird with its face toward the camera. The body holds still and the wings flap. It has heavy keylines and a flat, saturated orange, more cel-shaded than the grounded south/east. There is no twig.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a bulky four-legged beast seen head-on, with a tall curved horn rising from the middle of a plated, wedge-shaped head and a broad chest. Its legs end in hoof-like toes. East: a long, heavy quadruped in side profile walking right. A row of overlapping stone slabs runs down the back like shingles, and a big curved rhino-like horn rises from the head above a hooked, beak-like snout. A plated, spiky tail hangs at the rear. North: the rump, a segmented plated tail hanging down the middle, the back slabs in rows, and the horn tip showing above the back. No face. The whole body is covered in grey-brown stone plates with dark outlines, crossed by bands of orange. The orange is a flat burnt orange with little glow.
observed.south.png: Front view. The horned head faces the camera, with small dark eye slits under brow plates. Grey stone plates alternate with orange bands across the shoulders and legs. The legs are thick pillars with blunt toes. Clean alpha. Detail is moderate, and the outlines are fairly dark and even.
observed.east.png: Side profile. A heavy barrel body and a shingled stone ridge along the back. The head has a curved horn and a beaked snout. Broad orange bands run around the body in stripes. The underbelly between the legs is a darker, smoother grey-brown area with less visible plate division. A plated tail droops at the left. Clean alpha. Four legs with toes.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Rows of plates over the haunches, a plated tail hanging down the centre, and the horn tip curving up above the back. Orange bands cross the rump and legs. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Max zoom at 60 px/cell (the panel notes the art's native density is 47 px/cell). The beast is roughly 4–5 cells long and about 3.5 times the human's height: true megafauna. At 32 px/cell it still reads as a large horned quadruped with grey and orange banding against the ground. The art is somewhat soft at max zoom, with the plate texture slightly blurred.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rump, the hanging plated tail and back slabs. Only the horn tip shows above the back. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are at the game's angled camera, with no top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Heights measured at 191/191/193 px, a 1% spread. They look matched in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Horn, plated tail, back slabs and orange banding appear on every facing. The horn turns correctly: upright from the front, curved forward in profile, and its tip seen from behind on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The banded mineral plates are clear. But the feature the description names, glowing 'brighter at the seams between its plates' with stored heat, is not legible. The orange is broad, flat, matte bands (strata colour), while the actual seams between plates are dark outlines. Nothing reads as an emissive ember glow.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is rhino-like (horn, bulk, stance), but the shingled stone back, beaked head, plated tail and mineral banding push it well away from a rhinoceros. It reads as a rock-armoured creature, not a recoloured rhino.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 (separate stone-like plates): present. 2 (horizontal strata of differing mineral colours across the whole body): present, grey and orange bands everywhere. 3 (seams glowing bright ember-orange): weak or absent. STYLE.seen: Painted texture on the plates with reasonable shading. Not cute: no glossy eyes. The outlines are a little heavy and uniform, which leans toward illustration rather than vanilla painterly, but it is not cel or toy-like.

OURS.seen: A bespoke invented creature, the mod's own texPath under Pyrelands. Not a vanilla or donor animal.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha is present on all facings. No ground patch, shadow or backdrop.

SCALE.seen: About 3.5 times human height and 4–5 cells long, which fits 'megafauna'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a big horned, banded quadruped. The grey and orange contrast separates it from the ground.
